NASA Space Apps 2026 · Flame in Freefall

Which NASA microgravity fire experiments speak to your spacecraft atmosphere?

Moon and Mars vehicles plan to run at lower pressure and higher oxygen than the ISS, which makes materials burn more readily. Pick a cabin atmosphere: Flame in Freefall ranks NASA's flight investigations by how directly their data covers it, states what the flight tests measured there (each figure linked to the source row), estimates droplet-flame outcomes with a validated model, and says plainly what the data cannot tell you.

3 · What the flight data says here

Measured = computed from flight-test rows · Model estimate = validated FLEX model · Coverage gap = not covered. Click a test ID to see its source row.

Lower oxygen, more self-extinguishing droplet flames

Measured

In FLEX, 82% of 38 droplet flames at O₂ below 0.16 ended in extinction, versus 11% of 71 at O₂ of 0.30 or more.

  • Raw shares: pressure, diluent and droplet size also differ between these groups; the outcome model separates their effects.
  • Evidence lists a sample of the tests' recorded end states (4 per group).
Evidence:test 0031test 0034test 0047test 0052test 0188test 0192+2 more
Explain with cited sources

Reduced-pressure droplet tests

Measured

24 FLEX tests ran at or below 76 kPa (exploration-like pressure); 54% ended in extinction, versus 33% of 142 tests near 1 atm.

  • Oxygen fraction was not held constant between these groups.
  • Evidence lists a sample of the tests' recorded end states (4 per group).
Evidence:test 0209test 0211test 0216test 0220test 0075test 0078+2 more
Explain with cited sources

Flight tests closest to: ISS cabin (nominal)

Measured

58 FLEX droplet tests were flown within ±0.03 O₂ and ±25% pressure of this atmosphere (0.21 O₂, 101.3 kPa): 31 completion, 9 disruption, 18 extinction.

  • Droplet combustion only; spacecraft materials are mostly solids.
Evidence:test 0101test 0102test 0104test 0107test 0110test 0113+2 more
Explain with cited sources

Solid-material burns and enriched oxygen

Measured

BASS-II burned 63 solid samples (19 distinct material descriptions in the table) at initial O₂ 0.209–0.500. The scenario's O₂ lies inside that range.

  • The BASS-II table records conditions but no spread rate or extinction outcome; outcomes are in its videos and summary report.
Evidence:test 41test 42test 47test 48
Explain with cited sources

Outcome model estimate for this atmosphere

Model estimate

For a 3.00 mm droplet with no added diluent at 0.21 O₂ and 101.3 kPa, the FLEX outcome model gives Heptane: 55% burned to completion, 31% self-extinguished, 14% droplet disruption; Methanol: 48% burned to completion, 40% self-extinguished, 12% droplet disruption.

  • Model flex-outcome-rf-1.2.0: macro-F1 0.71 (baseline 0.29), extinction ROC-AUC 0.89; droplets only.
  • Evidence lists the nearest real flight tests and their recorded end state.
Evidence:test 0102test 0104test 0107
Explain with cited sources

What this flight data cannot tell you

Coverage gap

Every flight test here ran in microgravity; none ran at lunar (1/6 g) or Martian (3/8 g) gravity, so partial-gravity flame behaviour is not covered. BASS-II records test conditions but no outcome in its tables.

5 · Not covered yet

Shown so nobody mistakes an absence of data for an absence of risk.

  • SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III): registered, but its flight data has not been ingested yet.
  • ACME-CLD (Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame): registered, but its flight data has not been ingested yet.
  • Partial gravity. Every flight test here ran in microgravity; lunar (1/6 g) and Martian (3/8 g) flame behaviour is not covered.
